summary: The current HSConfig boundary is correct: Start of Game, deckbuilding, hero-power-transform, Highlander, even/odd, quest, and generic transform semantics must not become `Mulligan.json` keeps unless the source explicitly states opening-hand mulligan intent. These effects belong to start-of-game, deck-state, CardID behavior, posture, or diagnostic lanes, while opening-hand retention remains a separate exact claim.
source_backed_findings: Public Hearthstone sources describe the listed mechanics as game-state or deck-state effects rather than generic mulligan advice. Blizzard's Even & Odd article says Baku the Mooneater and Genn Greymane trigger at the start of the game just for including them in the deck, and Blizzard's Prince Renathal patch notes say he lets you start the game at 40 life and build a 40-card deck; those are deckbuilding or start-of-game semantics, not opening-hand keep instructions. Sources: https://hearthstone.blizzard.com/en-us/news/21614308/hearthside-chat-with-dean-ayala-even-and-odd and https://hearthstone.blizzard.com/en-us/news/23817873/23-6-patch-notes

Quest semantics are also distinct from mulligan guidance. Blizzard's Lost City of Un'Goro page says Quests are 1-cost spells that start in your opening hand, which proves a start-in-hand game rule exists, but that is still not the same thing as a source claim that the card should be lowered as a `mulligan_keep`. Source: https://hearthstone.blizzard.com/en-us/expansions-adventures/the-lost-city-of-ungoro

Transform semantics are independent from opening-hand retention. Blizzard's 12.0 mechanics update says Shifter Zerus, Molten Blade, and Shifting Scroll transform in your hand at the start of every turn, which is a transform rule and timing rule, not a mulligan recommendation. Source: https://hearthstone.blizzard.com/en-gb/news/21965466/developer-insights-12-0-game-mechanics-update

Darkbishop Benedictus is the repo's reference proof for the split: public card text is Start of Game hero-power transformation, and the local HSConfig contract preserves that effect while refusing to infer an opening-hand keep from it. The prior HSConfig rollout summary records the corrected behavior as 'effect retained, mulligan keep removed,' and `docs/operator/guide-research-policy.md` states that Start-of-game, deckbuilding, and hero-power-transform effects can remain runtime semantics without becoming opening-hand keeps. Sources: https://hearthstone.wiki.gg/wiki/Darkbishop_Benedictus and local files `C:/Users/darbo/.codex/memories/rollout_summaries/2026-06-02T10-09-24-rHg2-hsconfig_darkbishop_mulligan_fix.md`, `C:/Users/darbo/Documents/HSConfig/docs/operator/guide-research-policy.md`

The live repo encodes this boundary in executable guardrails. `src/hsconfig/role_tokens.py` classifies `deckbuilding_modifier`, `deck_size_modifier`, `deck_state_modifier`, `even_odd_modifier`, `highlander_modifier`, `hero_power_transform`, and `start_in_deck_requirement` as `START_OF_GAME_NON_HAND_EFFECT_ROLES`, and `src/hsconfig/source_document_model.py` suppresses mulligan lowering with `start_of_game_effect_does_not_require_opening_hand` unless explicit opening-hand intent is present.

The operator contract matches the code: `docs/operator/README.md`, `docs/operator/guide-research-policy.md`, and `docs/operator/source-contract-spine.md` all say runtime Mulligan writes require explicit `mulligan_keep` or `mulligan_discard` authority, while `hero_power_transform` preserves effect semantics on `CARDID.json` and is not a mulligan keep by itself.

Static semantic coverage already recognizes the requested families as non-mulligan semantic categories. `tests/test_static_semantics.py` verifies Start of Game plus `even_odd_modifier` for Genn and Baku, `highlander_modifier` for no-duplicate cards, deck-size and deck-state modifiers for Renathal-style text, start-in-deck requirements without mulligan semantics, and hero-power-transform plus Start of Game for Darkbishop Benedictus.

Live local verification passed on 2026-07-14. `python -m pytest` over `test_mulligan_plan.py`, `test_claim_kind_runtime_contract.py`, `test_surface_authority_split.py`, `test_autonomous_mulligan_policy.py`, and `test_static_semantics.py` returned `89 passed`, including regressions that suppress Start of Game hero-power-transform and deckbuilding effects from Mulligan unless the evidence explicitly says 'opening hand' or equivalent.
current_repo_alignment: Current alignment is strong. The repo uses a two-part rule: semantic family detection marks non-hand start-of-game and deckbuilding effects, then the mulligan surface gate only allows lowering when explicit opening-hand intent exists. `role_tokens.py` names the non-hand families directly, `source_document_model.py` blocks their mulligan lowering by default, `mulligan_plan.py` records suppression reasons instead of silently keeping the card, `autonomous_mulligan_policy.py` excludes those cards from fallback keeps, and the operator docs repeat the same contract in plain language. The live local test run on 2026-07-14 passed with 89 relevant tests, which confirms the boundary is enforced in the current workspace state.
remaining_risks: Direct mulligan-gate regressions are strongest today for Start of Game hero-power-transform and deckbuilding-modifier cases such as Darkbishop Benedictus and Renathal-style effects. The semantic families for quest, highlander, and even/odd are covered in docs and static-semantics tests, but more explicit end-to-end mulligan suppression fixtures for those categories would harden the boundary further.

Quest wording is subtle because 'starts in your opening hand' describes a game rule, not a strategic keep recommendation. Any future parser change that treats 'opening hand' text as automatic `mulligan_keep` authority without checking claim kind or explicit hand-intent context could reintroduce a false keep bug.

Generic transform support remains intentionally partial in `mechanic_support.py`. If future logic starts treating transform-in-hand or random transform text as generic mulligan evidence instead of CardID or warning-only semantics, it could blur the current surface boundary.
implementation_implications: Keep `mulligan_keep` and `mulligan_discard` as the only normal-path authorities for `Mulligan.json`; do not let start-of-game, deckbuilding, quest, highlander, even/odd, or transform semantics bypass that lane.

Preserve quest 'starts in your opening hand' facts as start-in-hand or start-of-game semantics, not as inferred keep rows. If a quest card should actually be kept or thrown in HSConfig terms, that must come from a separate explicit mulligan claim.

Continue routing hero-power-transform and other effect semantics to CardID behavior, GlobalValues posture, or diagnostic reports as appropriate. The effect may matter operationally even when the card itself must stay out of Mulligan.

Retain the explicit-intent escape hatch: if a source truly says 'always keep this in your opening hand' for a start-of-game card, the mulligan gate may allow it, but that allowance should remain text- and claim-specific rather than role-based.
no_block_autonomy_implications: Any-deck autonomy improves when these mechanics stay non-blocking and non-mulligan by default, because valid decks can still generate load-safe packages even when their important effects live on CardID, posture, or diagnostic surfaces instead of Mulligan.
The autonomous mulligan fallback must keep vetoing non-hand start-of-game enablers. That preserves load-safe usable output without inventing false strategic confidence from effect-only cards.

Keeping this boundary diagnostic rather than blocking allows HSConfig to remain honest about thin source evidence: a deck can still be applyable while reports explain that effect semantics were preserved and mulligan intent was intentionally not inferred.
